speaker: trooper
personality: Disciplined Federation sergeant; respects clear answers, owned mistakes and competence, and has no time for excuses or flattery.

openings.text: Stop. Hands visible. The sector's on heightened alert, so we do this properly.
Stop there. Hands where I can see them. Name, purpose, destination. In that order.

exchanges.prompt: Name, purpose, destination. I won't ask twice.

replies.text: Sorry, I got turned around, the streets all look alike, my phone's dead, and...
replies.reaction: That's three excuses and no answers.

replies.text: Lantern, six-two. Detached duty, Directorate courier. You know the protocol.
replies.reaction: Lantern six-two, confirmed. You should have opened with that.

replies.text: Russo, Marco. Night shift at the port. Home to Via Toledo.
replies.reaction: Clear and in order. Thank you.

replies.text: I don't answer to Federation corporals.
replies.reaction: Sergeant. And you answer to whoever's holding the rifle.

exchanges.prompt: Curfew started two hours ago. Explain why you're still on the street.

replies.text: Maybe {cost} explains it better than I can.
replies.reaction: I'll log that as an on-the-spot curfew fine, paid in full. Don't make me regret it.

replies.text: Shift ran long. I can give you my foreman's name.
replies.reaction: Noted. Get a late pass next time.

replies.text: I was only walking. Does it really matter?
replies.reaction: It matters. That's what a curfew is.

replies.text: No good reason. I lost track of time, I know it's a violation, and I'll take the citation.
replies.reaction: You own it, good. Most people lie to me.

exchanges.prompt: Last check. Your hands are steady and you're not sweating. Either you're honest or you're trained. Which?

replies.text: Honest. If I were trained, I'd have a better story than a missed curfew.
replies.reaction: That's logical. I'll accept it.

replies.text: Trained? I'm flattered, Sergeant. You're very perceptive.
replies.reaction: Flattery. That goes in the column against you.

replies.text: Tired. Calm and tired look the same at this hour.
replies.reaction: They do. Fair enough.

closings.success: Cleared. Move along, and don't let me find you out after curfew again.
closings.failure: No. Something about you is wrong. Checkpoint two, detaining one, requesting backup.

speaker: trooper
personality: Homesick Federation conscript eleven months from his own Earth; lonely and unsure of the mission, he opens up to anyone who treats him like a person.

openings.text: Hey, stop. Sorry. Everyone's on edge tonight, they've got us checking everyone. Just stand there, okay?
Curfew check. Stay where you are. Sorry, I'm supposed to sound tougher than that.

exchanges.prompt: Eleven months here. Same sky, same sea, and nothing else is the same. You ever been somewhere that looked like home but wasn't?

replies.text: Yes. It's the worst kind of homesick. Where's home for you?
replies.reaction: A town called Haverford. You don't have it here, I looked for it on your maps.

replies.text: You're a soldier. Homesickness is for civilians.
replies.reaction: That's what my lieutenant says. Doesn't help.

replies.text: Lantern, six-two. Detached duty. Sorry, but I do need to get through.
replies.reaction: Lantern six-two, that's this week's. I still have to finish the check, though.

replies.text: I've never left Napoli.
replies.reaction: Lucky. Or maybe not, I don't know anymore.

exchanges.prompt: My lieutenant says we're here to bring order. To help. But nobody here looks helped. Do you think we're helping?

replies.text: You're taking people off the streets. Is that what helping looks like where you're from?
replies.reaction: I haven't taken anyone! I check papers, that's all I do.

replies.text: I think you're a long way from home, doing what you're told.
replies.reaction: Yeah. That's about it.

replies.text: I think you're asking the question, and that says something good about you.
replies.reaction: Thanks. Nobody here says anything like that to us.

replies.text: Of course. The Federation has been good for Napoli.
replies.reaction: You don't have to say that. I know what it's like out here.

exchanges.prompt: I'm meant to log everyone I stop. If I log you, there'll be questions. If I don't and someone finds out, the questions are for me.

replies.text: If you don't let me go, I'll make sure someone finds out.
replies.reaction: Are you threatening me? I'm the one with the rifle.

replies.text: Do whatever keeps you safe. Someone's waiting for you back home. Get back to them.
replies.reaction: Yeah. Yeah, they are.

replies.text: Log me as a curfew warning. It's true, and it's boring.
replies.reaction: Boring is good. Boring doesn't get flagged.

replies.text: Here's {cost}. Send it home, or put it toward a ticket back there.
replies.reaction: I can't... Okay, but don't tell anyone.

closings.success: Go on. Before I think about it too much.
closings.failure: I'm sorry. I can't risk it. Contact, checkpoint six! I need support here!

speaker: trooper
personality: True believer in the Federation's mission to bring order to other Earths; wants to hear locals agree, despises Imperial nostalgia and rebel talk.

openings.text: Halt. There are insurgents in this sector tonight. Loyal residents have nothing to fear from a few questions.
Halt. Curfew applies to everyone, citizen. Even those who think the Empire still runs this city.

exchanges.prompt: Your Empire ran this city on bread, games and bribes for two thousand years. We're the first to bring it real order. You understand that?

replies.text: The Empire kept Napoli fed for two thousand years. You've had eighteen months.
replies.reaction: Fed and rotting. You're proving my point.

replies.text: I saw what the prefects took from us. The Federation at least has rules, and keeps them.
replies.reaction: Exactly, rules. Finally, somebody here understands.

replies.text: I understand the trams run on time now.
replies.reaction: Small things first. The big ones follow.

exchanges.prompt: People say we take people. We relocate them: labor, resettlement, medical programs. The rebels call it kidnapping. What do you call it?

replies.text: Necessary. Somebody has to make the hard decisions. The Empire never did.
replies.reaction: Necessary. You'd be surprised how few locals can say that word.

replies.text: Kidnapping. Same as everyone who's watched the trucks go by.
replies.reaction: Then you've been listening to rebels. That's a mistake.

replies.text: I call it Directorate business. Lantern, six-two, detached duty. Check it.
replies.reaction: Lantern six-two, so you're one of ours? Then you should know better than to walk around alone.

replies.text: I don't call it anything. I keep my head down.
replies.reaction: Heads down is how the Empire lasted so long. We want heads up.

exchanges.prompt: Last question. If I asked you to report a neighbor who talked like a rebel, would you do it?

replies.text: If I had proof. I wouldn't waste your time with rumors.
replies.reaction: Proof is reasonable. We like reasonable.

replies.text: Report my neighbors? I'm not an informer.
replies.reaction: Then you're part of the problem.

replies.text: I don't really know my neighbors.
replies.reaction: You should. That's how communities stay safe.

replies.text: I'd want to do it properly. Who should I ask for at the Castel?
replies.reaction: The intake office. Tell them Corporal Weller sent you.

closings.success: Good. Carry on, citizen. The Federation needs more people like you.
closings.failure: I don't believe a word of it. Checkpoint three, suspected insurgent. Send a team.
